narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 45% chance that you would become a bad credit risk. Although that is less than half, it was above the bank’s cutoff for approval, so the loan was not granted.

The strongest influences were the requested amount, your checking account status, and your installment burden. The requested amount was the most influential factor overall, but it actually worked in your favor: at 2,712 DM, it was below the approved average of 3,019.64 DM. Your installment burden also helped, since 2.00 was below the approved average of 2.99, suggesting your repayment would take a smaller share of disposable income.

The main reason for denial was your checking account status. A balance below 0 DM is a strong warning sign; among approved applicants, 59.2% had no negative balance, while only 12.6% had a negative one. That negative checking history pushed the prediction toward bad credit and outweighed the favorable amount and installment burden.

To improve your chances next time, focus on bringing your checking account into positive territory and keeping it there for several months. Reducing other debts and showing steadier savings would also help. You could then reapply, perhaps with a shorter loan term or a co-signer, once your account history looks stronger.
